title: Cellular energy utilization and molecular origin of standard metabolic rate in mammals
funder: Not read: the publisher's HTML and PDF full text returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-21; the PubMed, Europe PMC and Crossref records list no funder, and Semantic Scholar lists no open-access copy.
result: Review with quantitative estimates for mammals in the standard state, read in the abstract. About 90% of oxygen consumption is mitochondrial, of which about 20% is uncoupled by the mitochondrial proton leak and 80% is coupled to ATP synthesis. Of the 80% coupled to ATP synthesis, about 25-30% is used by protein synthesis, 19-28% by the Na+-K+-ATPase, 4-8% by the Ca2+-ATPase, 2-8% by the actinomyosin ATPase, 7-10% by gluconeogenesis and 3% by ureagenesis.
